source_text.body:
Run an e-commerce store with a human-approved agent
An agent operates the author's own store, handling inventory monitoring, support triage, sales anomaly detection and review summaries, with human approval for money or high-stakes customer matters.
·
Jul 1, 2025
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The author says the agent runs on their own store in production and handles inventory monitoring, customer support triage, sales anomaly detection, and review summarization on its own. For anything involving money or high-stakes customer contact, it stops and sends the human a suggestion with reasoning or a drafted reply, and the human approves, dismisses, or edits before anything happens.
How it went
The post presents it as a working live demo and says the same system powers the landing-page chat, but it gives no performance metrics, savings, or error-rate results. Its stated limitation is that reorders, refunds, and complaints are not fully automated.
Worth knowing
The key catch is the approval boundary: it never spends money or makes customer-facing promises autonomously, even in production.
Try it yourself
with
Zapier Agents
Copy prompt
Set up an agent for my online store on [Shopify/WooCommerce/other] that checks [inventory levels daily], sorts incoming support emails into [categories like shipping, refunds, product questions], flags unusual sales spikes or drops, and sends me a weekly summary of new reviews. It may draft replies and reports on its own, but it must pause and ask me before issuing refunds, changing prices, or replying to angry or high-stakes customers. Show me a test run on [last week's data] so I can confirm it works.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/u_Broox864/comments/1v5iif6/i_built_a_humanintheloop_ai_agent_that_operates_a
